topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the scope, themes, and learning outcomes of the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They frame cancer as a breakdown of normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization driven by accumulated genetic changes, alongside experimental models used to study these properties.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathology, and behavior of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the histological, diagnostic, and clinical distinctions between benign, locally invasive, and metastatic tumors, illustrating how tumors progress and affect surrounding tissues.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification rules
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized naming conventions and exceptions used to categorize benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the local, systemic, and metastatic mechanisms through which tumors compromise organ function and cause patient mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine patterns of cancer incidence and tissue vulnerability across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the clinical signs of cancer and evaluate various population screening methods used to detect pre-malignant and early-stage tumors.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and practical information for upcoming sessions.
